evidence: DEDR 3999 explicitly labels Konda pāta ‘cloth’ as borrowed from Telugu and gives Telugu pāta ‘old, decayed; an old cloth, a cloth’. The proposed immediate donor is that existing Telugu cloth attestation, not the unrelated pāṭa ‘song’; the survey pāṭa preserves a retroflex spelling difference requiring review.

DEDR 665 explicitly marks Gondi rōkal ‘pestle’ as a Telugu loan and gives Telugu rō̃kali ‘large wooden pestle’. The survey rokal is linked to that existing immediate Telugu donor; the dictionary’s uncertainty about the Telugu word’s deeper derivation (including comparison with DEDR 672) is preserved and does not negate its explicit donor statement.

DEDR 865 explicitly labels Gondi erra ‘red’ (including Koya) as borrowed from Telugu and gives Telugu eṟṟa ‘red’. The survey Koya erra is linked to that existing colour-word donor, not the homonymous Telugu earthworm entry.

Existing parent *iH- represents subsection (a), not the today/still/small formations in later subsections.

DEDR 3986(a) documents the pal tooth family: Kodagu pallï, Malayalam pallu, Tamil pal, Malto palu, Kolami pal, Gadaba pal/pallū with plural palkīl, and Toda pas̱. Survey plural and final-vowel material (including palku, pālkill, pāldu) remains unchanged. Toda parse is a comparative correspondence to its distinctive s̱ reflex; Betta Kurumba pallə extends the comparison to a lect absent from this article. Subsection (b) toothstick compounds are excluded.

DEDR2020 gives Tamil/Malayalam cēṟu mud or mire, Kota cēr mud and Kannada kesaṟ wet soil/mud. These simple southern survey forms preserve the corresponding c-/s-/ts- and cēr-/kesar- shapes; minority-lect assignments are comparative extensions, not claims that each lect is individually listed. Source final central vowels and length notation are retained.

DEDR2412 explicitly gives Malayalam caḷi, ceḷi, ceḷḷa mud/mire alongside Tamil caḷḷal mud/slush. Mannan ceḷi and Kadar caḷi are close southern comparative matches with the same mud sense and retroflex lateral; their source distinctions are preserved.

DEDR2552 gives Tamil/Malayalam iravu, irā, rā night, Irula rāvu night, Malayalam iruṭṭu/iriṭṭu darkness, and Kannada iruḷ/iraḷu/iraṭu/irḷu night. The selected simple southern forms match the night/darkness family, including loss of initial i- and final-vowel variants. Darkness-form responses elicited as night retain that survey sense; compound rāpodu-type answers are handled separately.

DEDR4990 gives Tamil moḻi joint of wrist/knee/ankle, muḷi bodily joint and Malayalam muḻi knuckle/joint, alongside muḻaṅ kai elbow. The simple Mannan moḷi and Irula muḷi elbow responses select the joint stem with the elicited anatomical specialization; no hand component is supplied where absent.

DEDR4935 explicitly gives Tamil muṭṭu knee, elbow, knuckle and Malayalam muṭṭu joint/knee/elbow. The selected simple southern muṭṭɨ elbow forms match this joint stem, preserving final central-vowel spelling.

DEDR4995 explicitly gives Tamil/Malayalam/Kota/Toda muḷ thorn, Kannada muḷ/muḷu/muḷḷu, Kodagu muḷḷï and Tulu muḷḷu. The selected simple southern survey muḷ/muḷḷu/muḷḷɨ responses retain this lateral stem; minority-lect coverage is a comparative extension, with final vowels and gemination preserved.

DEDR45 directly gives Kurux acc thorn alongside Malto acu. Survey atc/atca/atcɛ/atcʰɛ are close same-language affricate-transcription and final-vowel variants; the aspirated spelling is preserved rather than normalized in the source record. The more divergent ɛcʰ response is excluded.

DEDR2468 explicitly gives Konda sāmbu (plural sāpku) thorn, with Gadaba sāpu/sappu and Gondi sāp/hāp comparanda. Survey sāmpu and sāmu match the Konda nasal cluster, with devoicing or loss of the stop; these are stated survey variants rather than exact quotations.

DEDR3538 gives Tamil tōkai tail, Malayalam tōka, Kannada tōke, Gondi tōkār/tōkor/tōkar/tōka and Konda tōka tail. Selected simple survey tok-/tōk- responses match this family, retaining gemination and lect-specific final vowels. Gondi teke and other more divergent responses remain unassigned.

DEDR2594 explicitly gives Parji cind/cinḍ son, Ollari Gadaba sinḍ and Gadaba S. cinḍu/sinḍu son. The survey sīnḍu/cīnḍu responses match those same-language stems, with vowel length preserved; the child noun belongs to the documented small/young family.

DEDR1411 explicitly gives Kurux xaddas son/boy, xadd child and Malto qade son. Survey hatdas/xatdas/xatdɛś preserve the child stem and masculine ending with td/dd and initial h/x notation; the current **kaṯVtV reconstruction is used for that attested family, not inferred from resemblance alone.

DEDR4616 explicitly gives Tamil makaṉ and Malayalam makan/mōn son, Kannada maga/makan, Tulu mage and Toda mox child/son. The selected southern survey makan/magan/maga/mahan-type responses preserve the family, including k/g/h variation and nasalized or nasal-cluster lect forms. These minority-lect assignments are comparative proposals; ambiguous contractions and longer compounds are excluded.

DEDR4764 gives Gondi marrī/mari/marr son and Konda maṟin/maṟisi son (the latter referring to third person). Survey mar/maru and marisi/marsi retain these stems and the Konda relational ending, including syncope; ordinary inflection is not treated as derivation.

DEDR131 explicitly gives Tamil/Malayalam aṇṇan, Kannada aṇṇa/aṇa, Kodagu aṇṇë, Tulu aṇṇe and Konda ana/anasi elder brother. These complete survey forms match that kinship family, retaining final vowels and the Konda relational ending. Nursery-word similarity and the cited Prakrit comparison limit claims about the precise transmission history; compounds and unrelated brother terms are excluded.

DEDR23 explicitly gives Kannada akka elder sister, Kodagu akkë, Tulu akka/akkè, Telugu akka and Gondi akkā/akka with lect-specific sister senses. These simple southern and Gondi survey forms fit that kinship family; the nursery-word character and Sanskrit/Prakrit comparison do not by themselves establish a borrowing direction. The complete survey form and elder-sister sense are retained.

DEDR183 explicitly gives Tamil ammā, Malayalam amma, Kannada amma/ama, Telugu amma and numerous other mother/honorific uses. The selected survey amma/ammā mother responses belong to this nursery-word family. The Sanskrit ambā comparison and independent nursery-word formation limit the historical claim; no immediate borrowing direction is asserted, and lects using amme for father remain separate.

DEDR273 gives Kannada avva/avve/abbe mother, Kota av, Kodagu avvë and Gondi avva/avā/avval, with Tamil avvai and Telugu avva. These complete southern survey avv-/abb-/auv- responses fit that mother kinship family, retaining source vowels. The Prakrit avvā comparison and nursery-word character leave the exact transmission history open; divergent Irula agg-/aŋg- forms are excluded.

DEDR4616 explicitly gives Tamil makaḷ daughter, Malayalam mōḷ, Kota mōḷ, Kannada magaḷ, Tulu magaḷu, Parji māl and Gadaba māl. The selected survey makaḷ/magaḷ and shortened maka/maga/maha forms are comparative daughter extensions, with southern k/g/h variation and loss of final lateral; Parji/Gadaba māl/malu/melu preserve the separately documented central-Dravidian shape. Source gender/sense and vowel notation are retained; compounds and opaque contractions remain unassigned.

DEDR4481 gives Tamil/Malayalam poṭi powder/dust and Tulu/Telugu poḍi, alongside Kannada puḍi. The southern survey poḍi/pɔḍi dust responses match this simple powder stem, with source vowel notation retained; the Marathi comparison does not establish an immediate loan direction for these lects.

DEDR4316 gives Tamil puḻuti and Malayalam puḻuti dust, dry earth/powder. The selected survey puḷudi/puḷidi retain the full puḻuti-type stem and retroflex-lateral reflex; they are distinguished from the bracketed bhūti/būdi forms that DEDR explicitly considers possible Sanskrit loans.

DEDR3332 gives Kannada dumbu, Telugu dummu/dubba, Kolami dubba and Gondi dubā/ḍuba/dumu/dumul dust. Survey Irula ḍumbu and Gondi dummu/dubba fit this documented dust family; they are comparative lect matches, with no donor direction inferred from the neighbouring Telugu forms alone.

DEDR3283 gives Tamil tūci/tūcu dust and Tulu dūsu fine powder/dūselů dust. These selected tūsi/tūśi/tūśɨ/dūśi-type survey forms belong to that palatal/sibilant branch. Keep them separate from the dūḷi/dhūli branch explicitly identified in the same article as Sanskrit loans or contact-influenced forms; precise minority-lect history remains a comparative proposal.

DEDR72 gives Tamil/Malayalam aṭi bottom/base, Kannada aḍi under/bottom and Kodagu aḍi below/down. These simple or locatively inflected southern survey aḍi responses preserve that spatial use; aḍil/aḍiyil/aḍīle and aḍikkɨ retain their case endings and are ordinary inflections rather than separate derivations.

DEDR1619 gives Tamil/Malayalam kīḻ below, Kannada kīḻa/keḷagu, Kodagu kïḷï/kïda, Parji kiṛi and Kurux kiyyā beneath. Selected southern kiḷ-/kiś-/kɨg-/kɨh- survey variants and Parji/Gadaba kīḍi(n) are comparative extensions of that lower/below stem; Gadaba is supported comparatively by neighbouring Parji, not directly named in the article. Kurux kiya/kiye retain source final vowels; longer uncertain formations are excluded.

DEDR3805 explicitly lists Parji pokka/pokkai morning and paŋga dawn/morning under the day/daylight family. Survey pōkā is a same-language vowel-length and consonant-length variant, preserving the elicited morning sense.

DEDR3805 explicitly gives Kurux pairī morning and pahpahrnā to dawn. Survey pɔīrī retains the diphthong with a more rounded first component; this is a same-language comparative proposal. The longer pāīrī-bīrī response is excluded pending analysis of its second member.

DEDR5475 explicitly gives Tamil veṭiyal/viṭiyal break of day or dawn, from veṭi/viṭi to dawn. These southern survey vɛḍiyalɛ/vɛḍiyala/bɛḍiyalɛ morning responses preserve the nominal dawn formation, including initial v/b and final vowel variants; they are comparative minority-lect extensions. Questioned Kota/Toda comparisons in the article are not used.

DEDR1041 explicitly gives Tamil ōṭu, Malayalam ōṭuka, Kannada ōḍu and Kodagu ōḍ- to run. Survey Irula oḍu/oḍɨ and Alu Kurumba voḍu preserve the southern run stem, including initial glide and source inflection. The article’s explicit Telugu loan in Gondi and questioned Kui comparison are not used.

DEDR3582 gives Tamil naṭa, Malayalam naṭakka, Kannada naḍe/naḍi, Kodagu naḍa- and Tulu naḍapuni to walk. These complete southern survey naḍa/naḍi/naḍakk-/naḍap- forms preserve the stem and source inflection; the Kudiya naḍapu comparison follows intransitive Tulu naḍapuni, not Kannada causative naḍapu. Longer or opaque responses are excluded.

DEDR1835 gives Kannada kuḷir/kuḷḷir/kuḷḷu to sit down and Tulu kuḷḷuni to sit. Survey kuḷi/kulī, Badaga kuḷəvə and Tulu kullara retain that sitting stem with source inflections; auxiliary-bearing or longer kuṇḍuko/kuḷitiko responses remain separate.

DEDR3675 gives Kannada nil/nillu with nind- stem, Kodagu nill- with nipp-/nind-, Malayalam nilkka, Parji nilp-, Gondi imperative nillā and Kurux ijnā (ijjas) stand. Selected survey forms retain these ordinary stem/inflectional variants, including Kurux ījas and Badaga nippə; no extra auxiliary or causative analysis is inferred.

DEDR4850(a) explicitly gives Gondi M./Ko. mirr- run and M. mirānā flee. Survey mir/mira preserve that same-language run stem. The link uses the leap/run subsection, not the grasshopper noun subsection(b).

DEDR2950 gives Gondi ḍay- and ḍaiyānā flee. Survey dai/daiya elicited as run are close same-language variants with source non-retroflex notation; the flee/run semantic overlap is explicit. More complex or aspirated responses are excluded.

DEDR3151 explicitly gives Gondi tāk- walk across multiple lects, separately marking tākstānā/tāksahtānā as causatives. Selected takita/takna/takuda responses retain the simple walking stem with ordinary source endings; tāk-s- formations and fuller phrases are not reduced to this stem.

DEDR1769 gives Tamil kuraṅku, Malayalam kuraṅṅu, Kannada koraṅgi and Tulu kuraṅga monkey, with Kota korg/Toda kwarg. The selected southern survey koraŋg-/kuraŋg-/koraŋŋ- forms preserve that nasal-stop family, including Malayalam-type assimilation and final-vowel notation. The article’s explicit Tamil kōnti loan from Telugu is not used for these forms.

DEDR1769 explicitly gives Kannada kōti and Gadaba kōnti/kōti monkey. Survey koṭī/koṭe/konṭī retain those same-language forms with their retroflex/length transcription; no borrowing direction is inferred solely from the Telugu comparator.

DEDR2196 gives Irula kōḍa small monkey, Kota kōṛṇ small monkey, Kodagu kōḍë and Kannada kōḍaga monkey/ape. Selected koḍa/koḍɛ-type survey responses match the southern family; Kota kodunu retains its cluster with epenthetic vowels as a comparative variant. Keep the generic monkey elicitation sense distinct from dictionary species qualifications.

DEDR2142 explicitly gives Gondi kove/kovve/kōve/koye red-faced monkey. Survey kovi, kou̯e and kōβɛ preserve that intervocalic labial family, with vowel or fricative labial notation. The generic survey monkey sense is retained; species identity is not asserted.

DEDR2194 explicitly gives Konda kōnza red-faced monkey with Kui/Kuwi kōnja. Survey konja is a close same-language affricate/length variant; preserve the generic elicitation gloss without imposing a species distinction.

DEDR2830 gives Tamil cokkaṉ monkey and Malayalam cokkan monkey/dog. Mannan cɔkkan monkey is a close regional comparative match retaining its rounded-vowel notation; the source gloss selects the monkey sense.

DEDR4698 gives Tamil manti female monkey/monkey generally and Malayalam manti black-faced monkey. Muthuvan mandi is a close southern comparative match with intervocalic voicing; retain the survey generic monkey sense.

DEDR4004 gives Tamil/Malayalam paḻam ripe fruit, Irula pammu/pāmu, Toda pum, Kannada paṇṇu, Parji pal, Gondi paṇḍ(i) and Konda paṇḍu. Selected survey paḷam/payam/pagam/paśam/pām- responses preserve lect-specific reflexes or loss of the medial retroflex, and Kannada/related annu reflects loss of initial h-. These are comparative family proposals; the separate Indo-Aryan-looking phal forms and opaque responses are excluded.

DEDR1459 documents kāy/kāya green or unripe fruit throughout southern Dravidian and neighbouring Gondi kāyā fruit. Konda kāya is a comparative extension of that fruit stem; its survey generic fruit sense is retained and the evidence does not by itself establish borrowing direction.
DEDR1459 explicitly gives Kurux xańjpā/xańjkā fruit. Survey xhāñjpā preserves the same stem with its source initial-cluster and vowel-length notation; this is not the Indo-Aryan phal family.

DEDR3656 gives Tamil/Malayalam/Kota nāḷ day and Kannada nāḷ day/time. Selected southern survey nāḷ/naḷɨ/ṇāḷɨ retain this day stem; Mannan na is the proposed final-lateral-loss counterpart, qualified as a comparative lect extension. Longer temporal phrases are excluded.

DEDR3805 gives Tamil/Malayalam pakal day/daytime, Kannada pagal, Kodagu pōlï and Gondi pīal/piyāl/payal. Selected survey pakal/pagal/pahal and contracted pol/pīal-type forms retain those developments, with source vowels preserved. Generic day elicitation is kept distinct from the article’s daylight sense.

DEDR3656 explicitly gives Tamil nāḷai/nāḷaikku, Malayalam nāḷa, Kannada nāḷe, Kodagu nāḷe/nāḷēkï, Gondi nāṛ(i) and Kurux nelā tomorrow. Selected survey forms preserve the day-stem temporal/locative endings, including nāḷɛykɨ and regional vowel/lateral variants; these are ordinary inflected temporal forms. Opaque contractions and multiword temporal responses are excluded.

DEDR4753 gives Tamil maḻai, Malayalam maḻa, Kannada maḻe, Kodagu/Tulu maḷe, Kota may and Toda maw rain. These selected southern survey forms preserve lect-specific lateral, glide, velar or sibilant reflexes and contractions of the rain stem. Minority-lect assignments are comparative extensions; ambiguous source fragments and Indo-Aryan-looking varṣa forms are excluded.
DEDR4199 explicitly gives Konda piṟu rain, plural piRku, with Gondi pir/per and Kui piju. Survey piru retains the same Konda stem with source rhotic notation.

DEDR4199 gives Gondi pir/per/paṛ and L. peɣ rain. Selected pego/piu/pʸaɣu/pʸahu responses retain the documented rain family with velar/fricative or lost medial consonant and source glide notation; these are comparative lect proposals rather than exact quotations.

DEDR4240 gives Tamil pukai, Malayalam puka, Kannada/Kodagu poge, Tulu pugè/pogè, Telugu poga and Gondi poya/poyo/poī smoke. Selected survey p-/h-/zero-initial and intervocalic k/g/h/y forms preserve that family; voga/voge have a glide onset following initial-consonant loss. Source vowel and consonant notation is retained, while opaque longer responses are excluded.
DEDR2226 explicitly gives Konda gōyi kitchen smoke. Survey gōyu is a close same-language final-vowel variant; the questioned Parji/Gondi comparisons in this article are not used.

DEDR1391 explicitly gives Tamil kaṟi raw or boiled meat/vegetables and Malayalam kaṟi meats/vegetables/hot condiments. These southern survey kari meat responses select the meat sense of that culinary family, retaining the source non-retroflex rhotic spelling. Precise inter-lect transmission is not established by the widespread culinary term alone.

DEDR529 gives Tamil/Malayalam iṟacci, Kodagu eraci and Telugu eṟaci flesh/meat. Selected iraci/eraci and Betta Kurumba erusi/ərsi responses preserve the rhotic-plus-sibilant meat stem, including lect vowel change or syncope as comparative proposals; source spellings remain intact.

DEDR5345 explicitly gives Kannada bāḍu flesh, Kota vāṛ- small meat pieces and Tamil vāṭṭu roasted/fried flesh or vegetables. Selected Kannada/Alu Kurumba bāḍu/bādu/boḍɨ and Badaga pāḍə match that food noun family. Use5345, not the neighbouring wither verb5342 cited alongside it in the parsed Kannada dictionary.

DEDR2773 explicitly gives Parji cep flesh/game, plural ceppul, alongside Naiki cep/ceppu and Gadaba seppul. Survey cɛp is a same-language vowel-transcription match, with the generic meat elicitation sense retained.

DEDR5297 gives Tamil/Malayalam vaḻi way/path and Kannada baḻi way/road. The selected southern survey vaḷi/vaśi/vagi/vayi/veyi/bayi responses preserve lect reflexes or loss of medial ḻ and initial v/b variation. These are comparative minority-lect extensions; longer phrases and English road responses are excluded.
DEDR3024 gives Tamil taṭam road/path/route/footstep, Irula daḍḍa road and Kota daṛv path. Survey taḍam/tadam are close southern comparative matches, retaining source voicing and spacing.

DEDR3170 explicitly gives Kannada dāri road/path, Tulu/Telugu dāri and Tamil tāri. Selected Kannada and Alu Kurumba dāri/dārɨ/dāḷī/dārḷī retain the rhotic/lateral path stem; the lateral variants are comparative proposals. Tamil tārai is explicitly borrowed in the article, but that statement does not establish a donor route for these selected forms.

DEDR1184 explicitly gives Tamil kaṇṇi rope/neckrope, Kannada kaṇṇi rope/cord and Kota kayṇ yokerope. These simple southern survey kaṇṇi/kanni and Irula kəinni rope responses match the documented rope noun, with retroflex/gemination/vowel spelling retained; no eye-word parent is substituted.

DEDR1254 gives Tamil kayiṟu, Malayalam kayaṟu rope/cord and Kodagu kērï. Selected survey kayir-/kavar-/kagar-/kahar- forms are proposed comparative lect reflexes of the same rope stem, preserving intervocalic glide, labial, velar or fricative notation. More divergent Muthuvan kadɨrɨ/kadarɨ responses are excluded pending stronger sound evidence.

DEDR5305 gives Kannada baḷḷi/boḷḷi, Tulu baḷḷů and Koraga baḷḷi rope, alongside Tamil vaḷ/vaḷpu thong. Kudiya baḷḷi and Urali vaḷḷi are close southern comparative rope matches; the initial b/v difference and lateral gemination are retained.

DEDR449 gives Tamil iṭai/iṭam left, Malayalam iṭam/eṭam, Kannada eḍa and Kodagu ëḍate left. These selected simple southern iḍat-/eḍat-/iḍa/eḍa responses preserve the left-side family and ordinary adjectival endings. Longer side/hand compounds and Indo-Aryan ḍāva/ḍebri-type terms remain separate.

DEDR5276 gives Tamil valatu right side, Malayalam valam right side, Kannada bala, Kodagu balate, Telugu vala and Parji vela key right hand. These simple survey vala-/bala- forms preserve the strong/right family and source adjectival endings. Parji velā is the right-side stem without hand; correctness-sense sariyāna responses and longer compounds are excluded.

DEDR5259 gives Tamil vayiṟu, Malayalam vayaṟu, Kota vīr and Toda pīṟ belly, with Kannada basaṟu comparanda. Selected southern survey vayar-/vagar-/bagar- and contracted vēr-/vār-/bēr- forms preserve this belly family; minority-lect assignments are comparative extensions retaining source vowels and consonants, not separate claimed dictionary attestations.

DEDR3898 gives Tamil paṇti/paṇṭam belly/paunch and Malayalam paṇṭi stomach. Selected Kadar paṇḍam/panḍa and Muthuvan/Urali paṇḍi retain the same southern belly noun with source voicing/final-vowel notation. The Sanskrit lexicographical comparison alone does not establish an immediate donor for these forms.

DEDR4494 gives Kannada poṭṭe/poḍe/puṭṭi, Telugu/Parji poṭṭa and Gondi poṭa/poṭṭa belly. Kannada/nearby oṭṭ-/voṭṭ-/hoṭṭ- responses reflect initial p weakening/loss with glide or h onset; Gadaba puḍu/puḍḍu are neighbouring comparative voiced-stop forms. These proposed lect extensions retain source vowels; Prakrit poṭṭa comparison does not settle borrowing direction. The competing vaṭṭi-type family is explicitly excluded and held.

DEDR1892 gives Kannada kūdal hair, Tamil/Malayalam kūntal tresses, Tulu kujalů and Koraga kūdlu hair. Selected survey kūdal/kuḍulu and palatalized kunjulu/kūndzulu-type forms are comparative variants of this hair stem. The Sanskrit kuntala comparison is retained as a limit on precise transmission claims; no donor direction is asserted.

DEDR4707 explicitly gives Tamil mayir/macir hair, Malayalam mayir, Irula megaru/meguru/moyiru and Kota/Toda mīr. The selected simple survey magar-/masir-/mayir-/mehir-type forms preserve documented glide, velar or sibilant variation and source vowels; compound head-hair responses are analysed separately.

DEDR4921 gives Malayalam muṭi hair of head/top-knot, Tamil muṭi tuft/coil of hair and Kannada muḍi knot/bundle of hair. Selected simple muḍi hair responses retain this lexical hair noun; the broad survey hair sense is retained without silently adding a head component.

DEDR1973 explicitly gives Gondi kel hair/feather, plural -k. Survey kelk/kelku/kellku and kello retain that same-language hair family with source number/final-vowel and consonant-length notation. Ordinary plural morphology is not a separate derivation.

DEDR2002 gives Gadaba kenduṭ plural kendukul feather and kendī plural kendikīl/kendikūl, with S.3 kendiṭ hair. The selected kendukul/kendikīlu-type hair responses preserve the documented plural stems and hair/feather sense range; retain source voicing and final vowels as ordinary inflection.

DEDR1693 gives Kannada guṇḍige heart, Tulu guṇḍigè, Telugu guṇḍe/guṇḍiya and Gondi guṇḍe heart. Selected simple guṇḍige/guṇḍikɛ/guṇḍiyɛ/guṇḍa-type responses are comparative heart-family matches. Whole -kāy compounds are analysed separately rather than truncated.

DEDR3736 gives Tamil neñcu/neñcam heart, Malayalam neñcu/neññu, Kota nanj and Toda nïz. Selected survey neñcɨ/neñjɨ/nenji and Toda nic preserve this heart/breast family, with source vowel and final-affricate notation retained.

DEDR827 gives Kannada ede/edde chest/breast/courage and Tulu ede heart/chest, with Telugu eda heart. Kudiya ede, Badaga etə and Betta Kurumba yaddi are proposed comparative heart/chest-family variants, preserving initial glide, dental voicing and source sense.

DEDR839 gives Malayalam eluvu/eluṅku, Kannada elu/eluvu/elugu/emike/emake and Toda eḷf bone. Selected survey yeḷuvā/eḷuku/yelɨyɨ/yemke/yāmukɨ/yellu and Toda eṛḷf are comparative variants preserving source initial glides, vowels and lateral notation; the śelugū form is excluded pending an explanation of its initial consonant.

DEDR5050 explicitly gives Kannada mūḷe/muḷḷE, Kodagu mūḷe and Tulu mūḷe bone. These neighbouring southern survey muḷe/mūle/muḷɛ/moḷe/muḷa responses are comparative lect extensions with vowel/length notation retained. The article’s questioned Kurux muḍḍā comparison is not used.

DEDR2965 gives Telugu dummu, Konda ḍumu and Kuwi ḍumu bone. Gadaba dummu/dumme is a comparative extension of this regional bone family; final-vowel variation is preserved, and the evidence does not itself establish an immediate Telugu borrowing route.

DEDR2883 gives Tamil cōri/tōrai blood, Malayalam cōri/cōra and Kodagu cōre, within the pour/trickle family. Selected southern survey corā/cora/core/śorɛ/sɔ̄rē match that blood noun, preserving source sibilants and vowels. The more divergent śuvre response remains unassigned.

DEDR3748 gives Kannada nettar(u)/nettara/nettra, Tulu netterů and Gondi nettur/netur/nattur blood. Selected netter-/nettr-/naṭṭr-type survey responses preserve that stem with vowel variation or syncope; opaque Gondi naktur/naktar responses are excluded pending stronger consonant evidence.

DEDR3559 gives Kannada tōl(u) skin and Gondi tōl/tōla/tōlu, plural tōlku and Ko. tolka. Badaga tōlə and Gondi tollka retain the skin/hide family; the Gondi number/length notation is preserved as ordinary inflection.

DEDR5276 explicitly gives Tamil valiya strong/big, Malayalam valiya great, Kannada bal(u)/bolu bigness and Kodagu ballyë great. These southern survey valiya/baliya/belliya-type big adjectives extend that documented family, retaining ordinary adjective endings and source vowel/length notation. The right-hand sense of the current parent is only one sense: its primary article directly supports bigness.

DEDR3491 gives Kannada doḍḍa big and doḍḍitu/doḍḍittu that which is large, Tamil toṭṭa big and Kota doḍ big/great. These survey doḍḍ-/toṭṭ- adjectives and ordinary neuter forms belong with that family; source voicing, gemination and final-vowel differences are retained.

DEDR1646 gives Tamil kuñci anything small, Malayalam kuññu/kuñci young/small, Kota kun small and Kannada gunna smallness, beside kunni young animal. Selected kuñj-/kuñc-/kunn- survey small adjectives are comparative lect extensions with ordinary adjective/neuter endings. The neighbouring child/young-animal senses are explicit in the article.

DEDR1646 gives Tamil kuñci anything small, Malayalam kuñci/kuññu small and kuññan boy, and Kannada gunna smallness. These survey kuñci/kuñji/kuñjavan/kuñjatɨ and kunna-type short responses use the same smallness adjective, including ordinary human/neuter endings; preserve the survey short gloss rather than replacing it with child.

DEDR2594 gives Tamil ciṉṉa small/little and Malayalam cinna small, cinnan a short man. Southern survey cinna/tsinna and neuter tsinnadɨ/tsinnutɨ short are comparative variants of that explicit small/short family, retaining source affricate notation and endings.

DEDR2594 lists Kannada cina smallness, cinna/jinna smallness and ciṇṇi/ciṇṇe smallness/shortness. Kannada survey sīnnā/sinnaḍu small retain this stem with the survey sibilant spelling and ordinary adjective ending; distinct sanna/sunna forms are not silently merged.

DEDR1851 explicitly gives Malayalam kuṟiyatu what is short and kuṟayuka diminish/be short, beside Tamil kuṟu short and kuṟai diminish. Survey kuriyadɨ and korañjadɨ match the adjective and reduced/short participial response; the original source forms and gloss are preserved.

DEDR1851 gives Konda kuṟi short and kuṟikan short man, and Kota kūr shortness of stature. Konda kurika and Kota kūrāidu are corresponding survey short responses, with their ordinary endings retained; the article’s questioned Kota koṇ comparison is not used.

DEDR1839 gives Tamil kuḷḷaṉ short man, Malayalam kuḷḷan/kūḷan short/stunted and Kannada kuḷḷu shortness, kuḷḷa a short man. Selected survey kūḷe/kuḷḷa/kuḷan short responses match that contracted shortness family; DEDR cross-refers to kuṟu but these use the specific kuḷḷam entry.

DEDR3738 gives Malayalam neṭuppam length and neṭukkam tallness, Tamil neṭiyoṉ tall person, Telugu niḍuda long, and Konda niṟi long/niṟikan tall man. These neḍuppam/neḍukkam/naḍiya/naḍiyatɨ and Konda nirika survey responses match the documented long/tall family with ordinary adjective endings and source vowel notation.

DEDR621 gives Irula uddya long, Kannada udda/uddi/uddu length or height, Kodagu uddatë long and Tulu udda long. Survey uddā/vuḍḍā/uddu/utta/uddaṭā long preserve that family, including the initial glide and ordinary final-vowel or adjectival variation; longer opaque elicitation responses are excluded.

DEDR754 explicitly gives Parji ūluvi, plural ūluvul/ūlukul plantain, beside Gadaba uluk/ulg banana. Survey ulubi and ulu match that same-language plantain stem with labial variation or loss of the final syllable; original forms are retained.

DEDR2943 gives Kurux ṭaṭxā mango and Malto ṭaṭge. Survey ṭɔṭxa/ṭatxa-type responses preserve the same-language mango stem with vowel notation retained. Slash-separated tetke/tetxe and the uncertain tatk?a reading remain unresolved.

DEDR4772 explicitly gives Gondi markā/marka/maẖka, Konda maRka, Parji medi and Gadaba maygil/mayggā mango. These survey mark-/mahk-/mak-, medi and maige responses match that specific mango family, retaining consonant weakening and final-vowel notation; the distinct southern mā-m family is not substituted.

DEDR4782 gives Malayalam māvu mango tree and māṅṅa mango fruit, Tamil mā mango and Kodagu māŋge. The selected simple māṅga/māṅṅa and māve survey responses are comparative southern lect variants of this mango family; complete -kāy and -paḻam compounds are represented separately.

DEDR1422 gives Gadaba kākal, plural kākasil brinjal. The survey kākale/kākali and kākasil/kāgesil eggplant responses preserve that same-language singular/plural family with source vowel and voicing variation; ordinary number morphology is not a separate derivation.
DEDR2822 explicitly gives Konda sēṟga brinjal, with Kui sēje/hēje and Kuwi hēya. Survey sēṛga eggplant matches that same-language stem and retains the source’s consonant notation.

DEDR205 explicitly labels Gondi arti/arṭi banana as borrowed from Telugu and lists Telugu araṭi. Survey arati matches that loan; point to the existing Telugu araṭi attestation as immediate donor, rather than directly to the reconstructed family.

DEDR2086 gives Tamil kotuku/kocu/kocuku mosquito, Malayalam kotu/kotuku and Irula kucune. Selected survey kosukɨ/kosuvu/kosuvi, Irula kusune/kusuna and kotuvu/kodugu match the documented velar/dental/sibilant variants. Extended kosukisi-type responses are excluded pending analysis of their additional material.

DEDR2705 explicitly gives Kannada soḷḷe mosquito beside Tamil cuḷḷāṉ a kind of mosquito. Survey soḷḷe/solla/salla/colla retain that southern mosquito stem with vowel, sibilant and lateral notation preserved.

DEDR3715 explicitly gives Gondi nulle biting insect/gnat and nulē/nūle mosquito. Survey nulle matches the same-language family and original mosquito sense; similarly sounding but less secure lulle is excluded.
DEDR3715 gives Parji nuṛñi mosquito. Survey nurnyi preserves that stem with the source’s rhotic/nasal spelling; the separate urnyil response remains unresolved.

DEDR3715 explicitly gives Kannada noṇa/noṇavu fly/housefly. Survey none is the corresponding nominal response, with its final vowel and source dental/lateral convention retained. The nearby nonga-type forms are not assumed to belong to this stem.

DEDR4098 gives Gondi bālo spider beside Parji bāla. Survey bāli/bhāli/bālu/bhāluḍu are same-family candidates preserving final-vowel and aspiration notation and the ordinary final ending; this is a comparative extension of the documented Gondi stem, not a claim that every survey variant is printed in DEDR.

DEDR3214 explicitly gives Kurux tiŋglī fly beside Malto tilṉgru. The survey tiŋgli/tiŋgili/tiŋali-type noun responses retain that family, including the source’s epenthetic vowel or cluster notation. Verb fly responses are treated separately.

DEDR533 explicitly gives Alu Kurumba īpi and Irula īppi fly. Survey yippi in Alu and Betta Kurumba is a comparative noun-family match with initial glide and gemination retained; the gloss here denotes the insect, not flight.
DEDR4312 explicitly gives Parji puṛut, plural puṛtil worm. The survey puḍut response retains that same-language worm stem with the source retroflex-stop spelling preserved.

DEDR4312 gives Kannada puḻu/puḻa worm. Survey uḷa represents the weak-initial worm noun, comparable with Kannada huḷa; preserve its initial consonant loss and original form rather than silently normalizing it.

DEDR4020 gives Kannada pāṟu leap/run/fly, alongside its h-/zero-initial causative comparanda. Survey hāru/hārōdu/aruta retain the intransitive fly stem and ordinary elicitation endings with initial p weakening; causative-looking or opaque extended forms remain unassigned.

DEDR4020 gives Malayalam paṟakka fly and Kodagu pār- fly, with Tamil paṟa/paṟapp- and Kannada pāṟu. These survey par/per/pāra/paṟakkuga/parappa verbal responses match that flight family with ordinary infinitival/stem endings and vowels retained.

DEDR4020 explicitly gives Gondi pari-/paṛi-/parrī- to fly and parītānā/porītānā. Selected pari-/pare-/puri- survey responses preserve that stem with ordinary inflection and source vowels. Full pronominal clauses and forms resembling the separately listed causative parrih- are excluded.

DEDR3730 explicitly gives Konda egṟi- with past -t- to fly as a bird. Survey egritad/egrideng retain that same-language verb with ordinary past/infinitival endings; no donor is inferred solely from the neighbouring Telugu eguru comparison.

DEDR707 gives Malayalam uṟaṅṅuka sleep, Kannada oṟagu/oṟaṅgu and Kodagu or- fall asleep. Selected survey uraŋguga/voraŋgiyadu/oragada/ora and contracted argu/ergu responses retain this sleep stem with ordinary elicitation endings and initial-vowel/glide notation. The Toda orkʰa response is excluded because its verbal versus nominal/causative interpretation remains unclear.

DEDR1407 explicitly gives Kurux xandrnā to sleep within the dream family. Survey xandaras is an ordinary inflected response based on that same-language sleep verb; the nearby kʰandavna form is excluded pending analysis of its internal consonant/possible extension.

DEDR3291 explicitly gives Gondi sunj-/hunj-/unj- sleep and separately marks causative hunjih-. Selected sunc-/hunc-/unj- survey responses match the intransitive sleep stem with ordinary tense/person endings. Full clauses beginning with pronouns and forms whose causative status is unclear are excluded.

DEDR3291 explicitly gives Konda sunz- with past -it- to sleep and the Sova variant sus-. Survey sunjitan and suja are same-language comparative responses retaining the sleep stem and ordinary ending/cluster simplification; the nidra construction is kept separate.
DEDR4652 explicitly gives Parji maḍ- with past maṭṭ- lie down/sleep. Survey maḍ matches that documented stem; the article’s explicitly Indo-Aryan Brahui maṭṭa is not used to infer a donor for Parji.

DEDR4652 gives Gondi minḍānā/mindānā, menḍanā and mīnḍ-/mīṛ- sleep. Survey mindu retains that same-language stem with source voicing and final vowel preserved. The more opaque minmudu response is excluded pending consonant-cluster analysis.

DEDR4735 gives Kannada malagu/malaṅgu recline/lie down and Tulu malaguni sleep. Survey malugu is the ordinary same-language sleep verb with unstressed vowel variation, not a compound or a borrowed nidra noun.

DEDR4652 explicitly gives Gondi minḍānā lie on one side and menḍanā/mīnḍ- sleep. Selected menḍ-/minḍ-/min- survey lie-down responses retain that stem with ordinary inflection and source cluster notation; longer auxiliary constructions are excluded.

DEDR1907(c) explicitly gives Konda gūr- with past -it- lie down/sleep/roll on floor, within the fall/roll family. Survey guritan and gura match this specific subsection with ordinary endings; the rain comparison in the article is questioned and is not the evidence here.

DEDR1097 gives Kannada kaccu bite and Tamil kaccu gnaw/nibble. Survey kacc-/kats-/kac- bite responses are comparative southern variants retaining the source affricate spelling and ordinary final vowels; the semantic fit is explicitly biting.

DEDR1097 explicitly gives Gondi kask-, kac- and kas- bite. These kask-/kac-/kats- survey responses preserve that same-language family with ordinary inflection and the source’s stop/affricate notation. Pronominal clauses and more opaque auxiliary expressions remain unresolved.

DEDR1124 explicitly gives Konda kaṭ- with past -t- bite/sting and separately lists kaṭis-/kaṭpis- cause to bite. Survey kattad/kata/katteng matches the base bite verb with ordinary past or infinitival endings, without assigning the separate causative.

DEDR1124 gives Tamil kaṭi, Malayalam kaṭikka and Kannada kaḍi bite. Survey kaḍi/kaḍikkuga preserves the documented southern bite verb with ordinary infinitival endings and source voicing; the unrelated cut entry d1125 is not substituted.

DEDR2164 explicitly gives Parji kork- gnaw/nibble and Gondi kork-/kōrkānā bite/nibble. Survey kork/koruku/korkodu retains that same-language stem with ordinary inflection and epenthetic vowels; no Telugu borrowing is inferred from resemblance alone.

DEDR3962(a) gives Kurux parᵃmnā to bite, also separate the halves of pulse with a handmill. Survey pormias/parimias matches that specific bite verb with ordinary inflection and source vowel variation; the separate subsection (b) chip/slice borrowing is not used.

DEDR5478 gives Tamil veṭṭu and Malayalam veṭṭuka cut, Tulu beṭṭuni cut and Kannada beṭṭu strike/impress. Survey beṭṭu cut is a southern comparative extension of this specific cutting family; the homonymous finger and hill entries found by homepage search are excluded.

DEDR3140 gives Kannada taṟi/taṟe cut/strip off, Tamil taṟi cut and Malayalam taṟikka cut down. Survey tāro cut is a proposed same-language stem variant with its imperative-like final vowel retained; it is not linked merely to a similar noun.

DEDR5354 gives Tamil vāyil/vāyal/vācal/vāytal doorway, Malayalam vātil, Kannada bāgil/bāgal/bākal, Tulu bādhaḷa and Kota vāl entrance door. Selected southern survey vāsa/vācal/bāsa/vātil/bādal/bāgalu and Kota vāl preserve the documented lateral, dental and sibilant variants and lect contractions. Full doorway-step compounds are kept separate.
DEDR5277 explicitly gives Gadaba val door, distinct from the neighbouring vāyil doorway article’s Gadaba vāl outside. Survey valu matches the door noun with its source final vowel preserved.

DEDR3845 gives Kannada paḍi panel/door, Kodagu paḍi door and Tulu paḍi bamboo door/shutter. Kudiya paḍi is a direct neighbouring-lect door-family match; the general door gloss is retained without imposing a construction material.

DEDR2646 gives Kannada cikki/cikke star, Gadaba sukka and Gondi sukkum/huko/hukka/ukkum/ukka/ukam star. Selected cukk-/sukk-/ukk- survey nouns preserve documented sibilant weakening, stem-final vowels and ordinary plural endings. DEDR explicitly marks Tamil cukkai as a Telugu loan; no Tamil response is included in this inherited-family proposal.

DEDR4876 gives Kannada mīn star within miṇa/miṇuku/minugu glitter and shine. Survey mɨnɨ/minna star retains this shining/star family with source vowels and ordinary endings. The identically sounding fish family is not used.

DEDR3213 gives Tamil/Malayalam tiṅkaḷ, Kannada tiṅgaḷ, Kota tigḷ, Toda tïgïḷ moon and Kodagu tiŋga month. DEDR3754 gives Tamil nilavu/nilā, Malayalam nilāvu/lāvu, Kodagu nelaci, Telugu nela, Gadaba neliŋ and Gondi nalenj/nelenj/lēnj moon. DEDR2287 explicitly gives Gondi jaŋo/jango moon beside Naiki jaŋgo. Survey jahŋgɨ/jaŋgō retain that same-language family, preserving the survey aspiration/consonant and final-vowel notation.

DEDR2599 gives Kodagu cīpe, Gadaba sēpe/cēpēḍ and Toda kīp broom, with the Tamil cī-/cīvu sweep family. Kudiya ceppe, Gadaba cip and Betta Kurumba kippi are comparative broom-family responses preserving source initial-consonant, vowel and gemination notation.

DEDR2599 gives Tamil cīvu to sweep clean and Malayalam cūl broom, beside cīprā/cīpari broom. DEDR2599 explicitly gives Gondi hēpur/hepur/ēpur broom. Survey hebru is a comparative metathesized and voiced-cluster form of this same-language noun; more opaque epuɣai/epoiyi responses remain unassigned.

DEDR4415 gives Tamil perukku and Malayalam perukkuka sweep with Kannada porake/parake broom. Survey perukku elicited as broom is a lect nominal use of this sweep/broom family; retain the nominal survey meaning rather than silently changing the gloss to a verb.

DEDR4794 gives Malayalam māccal/māccil besom/broom, Tulu maipu/māypu and Koraga māyi broom. Kudiya māci is a proposed neighbouring-lect match to the māccil-type stem with the shortened ending preserved. The article’s questioned Tamil māṟu comparison is not used.

DEDR2375 explicitly gives Kurux calkī broom or its special grass, alongside Malto celaki grass broom. Survey cʰelki matches that same-language broom noun with source aspiration and vowel notation retained.

DEDR1042 gives Tamil/Malayalam ōṭu and Tulu ōḍu tile, beside Telugu ōḍu-billa roofing tile. Irula ōḍu elicited for roof uses that tile word metonymically for the roof; preserve the source roof gloss and do not add an unattested house component.

DEDR4796(a) explicitly gives Tulu māḍů roof within the māṭam/māḍa building family. Kudiya māḍ is the same regional roof noun with its final-vowel loss preserved. The Sanskrit architectural comparisons do not by themselves establish a separate immediate borrowing route for this response.

DEDR1904 gives Tamil kūrai sloping roof and Malayalam kūra hut/thatch. Kannada survey kūrɛ roof is a proposed southern comparative roof-family extension with final-vowel notation retained; the article’s questioned Kolami comparison is not used.

DEDR3922 gives Tamil/Malayalam pantal and Kannada pandal temporary shed, and Kuwi pandri roof structure with thatch. Survey panḍal roof retains this shelter/roof-structure family; the broad elicited roof sense is preserved rather than replacing it with a wedding-specific use.

DEDR1395 gives Tamil kaṟu with past -tt- become black, kaṟuppaṉ black man and Kodagu karatë black. The selected karutta/karuttavan/karttatɨ/karettu responses retain the documented black adjective or human form and ordinary endings; the exact source black gloss is preserved.

DEDR404 gives Tamil āṟu with past āṟi- cool/grow cold, Malayalam āṟuka and Kannada āṟu grow cool. These āriya/ārin-/āriyad-/ārud-/āriyott- cold responses retain that cooling verb with ordinary participial/adjective endings and exact source spellings. Longer serial constructions remain unanalysed.

DEDR1568 explicitly gives Kurux kīrnā be cold/feel cold. Survey kiirna directly matches that verb with its doubled-vowel notation preserved.

DEDR1568 gives Gondi kiriŋ-/kirŋg- be cold and Koya kirŋ- become cool. Survey kirinted is a proposed same-language cold participle with its nasal/stop ending preserved; the more opaque iriŋgam response is not assigned.
DEDR1601 explicitly gives Gondi kinan/kīnd cold and kinnān wet/cool. Survey kina cold is a same-language truncated adjective response with its source final vowel preserved.

DEDR2056 gives Kannada kōṭa/koḍata coldness and kōḍu be cold, with Malayalam kōṭṭam coldness. Kodagu kōṭa cold is a neighbouring-lect comparative match, retaining the source vowel/stop notation.

DEDR601 gives Tamil uṇaṅku, Malayalam uṇaṅṅuka, Kannada oṇagu, Tulu oṇuṅgelu/uṇuṅgu/nuṅgu dry and dry up. These unag-/oṇag-/voṇag-/nuṅg- survey responses preserve that drying stem, ordinary adjectival endings and initial glide; potentially competing nānt-/nan- readings are excluded.

DEDR5320 explicitly gives Gondi vatt-/vat-/vas- dry up and wither, with separate causatives vatth-/vattih-/vasp-. Selected vat-/vart-/vast- survey dry responses retain the base dry stem and ordinary adjectival inflection; parenthetical or clearly extended responses are excluded.

DEDR3630 gives Tamil nanai wet with past -nt-, Malayalam nanayuka/nanaccal wetness and Kodagu nele- with past neland- get wet. DEDR445 explicitly gives Gadaba iḍigeda a few within the small/narrow family. Survey iḍigute/iḍigale is a same-language comparative variant with its source final consonant/vowel and ordinary adjective endings preserved.

DEDR2594 gives Tamil/Malayalam cinna small/little and Kannada cinna smallness. Irula cinnadɨ few is a comparative quantity use of that small adjective with its ordinary neuter ending; the source few gloss is preserved.

DEDR4127 explicitly gives Gondi puh-/puhtānā be heavy, with the wider Pengo/Kui pik- family. DEDR4791 explicitly gives Kurux mēt/mē̃t adult man, husband. Survey mētas/mētes/mētus matches that same-language stem with ordinary masculine -s and source vowels preserved; it is not assigned by resemblance to Indo-Aryan man words.
